«solo»: true, the character fights alone -- nobody joins, his heroes neither (one a side); false,
a group may. As the guides say, quest by quest: «Le combat se lance et s'effectue seul» against
Caporale Mynerve, «il peut se faire à plusieurs» against Rasamoune (Dofus pour les noobs first,
then JeuxOnLine, Dofuserie). Absent where no guide says: then the board decides, and one that
flags a single cell for the players is played alone (FightHandler.PlayedAlone).

«element» (no npc, no reply): the fight starts when that element of «map» is used, while the
row's «criterion» holds and its chain is not done; «type» is the interactive type it is shown
with meanwhile. «then»: the fight that starts as soon as this one is won and the character is
back on the map, a row of its own; the last one's «marks» closes the chain.
START CELLS. «playerCell»: the cell the character starts on; «allyCells»: one per «allies» entry
(0 leaves that ally to the board); «cell» in a «monsters» entry: where that monster starts. Each
is a cell of the arena's board (name the «arena» so the cells stay tied to it) and wins over the
board's placement; the cell joins its side's placement list, so the character may still move
there. A cell the board cannot be stood on is ignored and logged. Without them nothing changes.
A board whose placement gives a side no walkable cell places both sides on its own walkable
cells instead (logged once per board). «Le jour des assassins» (1936) starts the character
beside the magypus so it can be put to sleep in the first round.
